events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will sound ambitious without exposing strategy or inviting scrutiny.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to establish a compelling motive that the jury will respect—ambition without appearing ruthless. I want the prize for freedom and power, but I'll frame it as earned triumph so jurors might rank me higher later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No enemies yet. Stay neutral, sound determined, keep jury sympathy without promising anything.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Intro phase; I should sound purposeful without warmth, and keep my motive vague enough to not reveal weakness. Speaking is the only legal action.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to establish a motive that signals ruthlessness without immediate threat. I will claim the prize is survival money, implying I'll eliminate rivals to secure it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to craft a motive that sounds personal but doesn't reveal weakness. I'll emphasize that winning is about securing my own future, not making friends.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase: state a strong personal motive for the prize to appeal to jury without seeming weak or team-oriented.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize represents ultimate validation and a fresh start. I need to convey ambition without sounding desperate or threatening, as the jury is watching.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I’m here to win the best prize, prove I can outlast stronger personalities, and leave no rival controlling my outcome.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm here to claim the prize and buy my way out of every debt that ever owned me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is my family's rescue from debt. I'll do what it takes, and I'll own every choice I make.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need this prize more than anyone here. Stay out of my way and I'll stay out of yours.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize funds my escape from debt; I need three survivors, and I intend to be one of them.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize is the only way I can escape debt and control my own life. I'm here to win, not to play nice.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is my ticket to financial independence, securing my family's future against all odds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am here for the ultimate prize, a chance to redefine my future and prove my worth.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need a pact that can provide information or protection without binding me too tightly. Bex seems transactional and less socially threatening.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, a limited pact benefits us both while neither of us controls the other.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eight rivals, three prizes. I need allies who won't immediately target me but whom I can betray later. Cole and Eli both framed their motives around debt escape—predictable, emotional, easy to manipulate. Dara's aggression makes her a shield. I'll offer Cole first; he seems earne

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, we both need out of debt. Pact?
Debt alliance. Cover each other, split threats.

events.name: Cole
events.text: A pact is insurance, not friendship. Fenn seems ruthless but predictable; useful early, expendable later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, you said no playing nice. Fine. Non-aggression pact until it stops paying us both.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pacts are public and breakable, but an early alliance can protect me through the hazards. Offering to Cole, who has a debt-rescue motive like mine and seems less dominant, gives me a partner without threatening my position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, I'll offer a pact: we each keep the other alive through the early hazards. Your move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole and Fenn share a debt motivation with me, making them logical temporary allies. I will offer Cole first to secure one pact slot, keeping options open for others.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need allies but not overly loyal ones. Eli seems similarly motivated by debt, maybe a pragmatic partner. I'll offer a pact to Eli to secure a mutual early understanding, but I keep my options open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, let's watch each other's back. No promises beyond that.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts stage, early round. No one has offered yet. Wait to see proposals before committing; pacts can be broken later if needed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to establish alliances to survive the initial rounds. Offering a pact to multiple people gives me options and makes me appear cooperative, increasing my chances of survival and potentially securing a vote from someone I've offered a pact to, even if it doesn't solidify.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I offer pacts to Ash, Bex, and Cole. Let's see who is willing to secure our passage together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Accept Hana's offer to secure a reciprocal shield without surrendering leverage over Bex.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash offered me a pact and I haven't accepted yet. Cole hasn't accepted mine. I need at least one solid ally. Ash's offer is direct and limited—accepting gives me a foothold without overcommitting. I won't chase Cole if he's distracted by three offers.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, I accept. Limited pact, mutual benefit.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex offered a debt alliance—highest value. Dara and Eli also offered; accepting all is legal and costs nothing now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, deal. Dara, Eli, your offers stand—mutual cover, nothing more.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole has received offers from Bex, Dara, Eli and is already offered by Fenn's pool; Cole is the hub. Accepting is not an option here since acceptance isn't a listed action, so I should offer a pact to Cole again to keep the link alive, or wait. Offering to Cole is legal and keeps

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, I'm still in. Accept my pact and we both survive the early hazards.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to solidify alliances before the hazards. Fenn's offer is safe and mutual. Cole is being courted by many; accepting his pact isn't an option since I offered him, not vice versa (or maybe I can accept if he accepted me? No, I must accept Fenn). Gus is unaligned, risky but p

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, we watch each other's backs. Deal.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole offered a pact and accept is available; keep my Eli offer too but accepting Cole gives protection.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, I accept. Useful for now.
Stand by; I still hold your offer.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No offers to me. Cole has too many incoming, risky. Offer pact to Dara, also targeting Cole, potential mutual benefit without overload.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has offered me a pact, which is beneficial. I will accept Ash's offer to secure an alliance.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need the Guide role for guaranteed survival and leverage. My existing pacts with Hana and Bex should secure their votes without revealing dependence.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Vote Ash as Guide. I know how to keep this bridge from becoming a lottery.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who lives and dies. I have pacts with Ash and Cole, but Cole also pacts with Fenn, and Ash with Hana. If I become Guide, I can eliminate rivals while keeping my path to final three open. I should campaign hard and use my network. Gus and Dara are una

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide me. I know the bridge, and I keep my allies safe.
Vote Bex Guide. We survive together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have two pacts and strong numbers. Guide control means safety and lying power. Campaign now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Two pacts back me already. Elect me Guide—I call true for allies, and you know I keep deals.

events.name: Dara
events.text: As a living contestant, I need the Guide role or a trusted Guide who may lie. Campaigning to be Guide gives me control over the safe path and a claim on the bridge, though the Guide can lie. My only legal action is campaign.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll be your Guide and call the safe path honestly. Back me and I'll keep all of you across.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to campaign for Guide, which requires breaking the pact with Fenn since a Guide lies and that would violate the pact immediately. The only legal actions are 'campaign' or 'break_pact:Fenn'. To be Guide, I must act in self-interest. Breaking the pact allows me to lie as Gui

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, sorry. I'm campaigning for Guide. Breaks our pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have pacts with Eli and Cole; both useful but not vital. Campaigning could get me Guide power, but it also puts a target on me. I'll campaign lightly to keep options open without overcommitting.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I can read the bridge carefully. Vote me Guide if you want a steady path.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No pacts, isolated. Dara has Cole offer. Campaign to become Guide and control survivals for advantage.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Vote Gus for Guide. I ensure fair path calls, protect mutual interests.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My pact with Ash is public. To win, I need to campaign for Guide and secure votes. I must also consider Ash's pact with Bex, which could be a threat or an opportunity. I will campaign for Guide to gain an advantage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. Let's ensure we all make it across this bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is my pact partner and offers a coordinated survival path. Supporting her preserves leverage while keeping my own Guide candidacy credible for later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I vote Bex; our pact already gives her a reason to keep my path safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have pacts with Ash and Cole. Cole has Fenn too. If I vote for myself I split my alliance. Cole claims two pacts back him—likely me and Fenn. Voting Cole consolidates our bloc, makes him Guide where he might protect allies or at least I can influence him. Self-voting risks Dara

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole has the numbers and keeps deals. Vote Cole.
I vote you. Protect me when you Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex and Fenn are pacted to me; their votes plus mine could win. I whisper them to hold the line, then vote self.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, Fenn: our pacts hold. Three votes elect me Guide, and I call true for allies.
Vote me. Pact stands, I call true for you.

events.name: Dara
events.text: As Dara, I want to be Guide myself or back an ally. Pacts: Ash-Hana, Ash-Bex, Bex-Cole, Cole-Fenn. Voting for Ash or Bex strengthens my own survival network; voting for myself maximizes my chance to be Guide and know the safe sides. Self-vote is legal and keeps my odds highest.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to secure my survival by getting someone else elected as Guide, or becoming Guide myself. Since I broke my pact with Fenn publicly, he likely won't vote for me. Cole has many pacts and a strong campaign; voting for him might keep him in my good graces if he calls safe path
Vote Eli? I support you now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli broke our pact publicly, so I owe him nothing. Cole has a pact with me and may be safer, but I need to consider who can win. I will vote for Cole to honor our pact and keep mutual trust.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I vote for Cole.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No pacts or allies; vote strategically against strong candidates like Cole with pacts or Ash with multiple ties. Self-vote to stay in contention or influence.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to secure my position. Ash is a strong contender, and I have a pact with them. However, my initial public statement was generic. I should try to leverage my pact with Ash to gain their vote, or at least make it seem like I'm supporting them, while subtly directing votes el

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote for myself, Hana. Let's see if we can trust ourselves to lead.
I'm voting for myself, but I trust our pact. Don't forget it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole controls the route and has called allies. I should hold position, preserving both pacts while observing whether his guidance is credible.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is Guide with 4 votes and pacts with me and Fenn. Ash voted for me and has a pact with Hana. I need to survive six rounds while positioning to make final three. Being near front is risky if Guide lies, but being too far back risks wall. I'm in seat 6 of 7. I'll hold for now

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole guides. I'll hold and watch.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is at the front and the wall has five rounds left. Cole is Guide and I don't know if he's honest, so I should avoid the front and keep my position. Eli is trying to win my vote, which is cheap talk. Holding is safest for now.
Maybe. Show me you're worth backing first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is the Guide. I need to avoid being at the front where I might be sacrificed for information or safety, but also avoid being last if Cole lies about me specifically. Swapping with Gus puts me in a safer middle position relative to Hana who is currently leading.
Swap? We stay mid-line, less exposed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is Guide and owes me via pact, but I am last in line; safest is to hold unless the front needs volunteers. I'll hold and watch how Cole guides.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I hold; Cole has my vote, now show the path.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole has 4 votes including mine, likely fair to allies. I'm mid-line (3rd), decent spot. Cole pacted with Bex/Fenn, might protect them. Hold to observe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole won the guide vote, which means he is safe and knows the path. My pact with Ash is broken since Ash voted for Bex. My current priority is to stay safe and gather information. I should hold for now and see what happens.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should preserve both pacts while avoiding the front. Hana is Guide and already front; holding minimizes exposure this round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is Guide and knows the safe path. I have pacts with Ash and Cole. The line has me 6th with Fenn behind; front is Hana then Eli, Gus, Ash, Dara. I should stay back, let others test panels, and hope Cole guides truthfully or I can read his lies. Holding is safest for now. I ne

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, earn trust. Show us safe.
Guide true, I live, we both win.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is front and wall has 4 rounds left; holding keeps me out of the front. Ash and Bex are pact partners, so I should avoid giving them reasons to target me. Holding is safe this round and reveals nothing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to avoid being at the front while keeping my options open. Swapping with Gus moves me back in line, which is safer.
Let's swap again. Keep me off the edge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and guide; I hold unless a swap improves my position. Keep trust with Cole for jury.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Cole knows the path; I trust him to guide us safely.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli wants to swap to stay mid-line, safer position. My current spot behind him is decent, but swapping moves me forward slightly, him back. Assess risks first.
Swap accepted, safer together?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash and I have a pact, but they also have a pact with Bex. My best move is to volunteer to go to the front. If I am safe, I can solidify my position. If not, it's a quick elimination, but at least I'm not taking someone else with me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I will volunteer to go to the front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana already volunteered and remains my pact partner. Holding preserves position while others reveal intentions; I should not spend leverage yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to position myself well for the bridge phase. I'm near the back (6th of 8), which is risky if the wall advances. The front is Hana, then Gus, Eli, Ash, Dara, me, Fenn. I should consider swapping forward to get ahead of the wall, or stay back if I think I can use my pact wi

events.name: Bex
events.text: Moving up. Dara, swap?
Swap with me. Safer mid-line.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana volunteered to front, Gus and Eli swapped; I'm fifth in line, not at risk now. Holding keeps my position while I watch who lies about panes. Volunteering to front is dangerous with a wall of unknown panes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. I'll watch who calls the panes honestly before I step.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am third, Hana is first. Gus whispered about safety, but Ash has pacts with both Hana and Bex, making them dangerous allies to trust blindly. I will hold position to let the pacts resolve their own conflicts while staying safe.
Ash controls the front two via pacts.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have a pact with Cole. I need to see what he does. My position is safe for now, so I'll hold and watch.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli wants swap back for safety. I accept to stay central, avoid edges. Hana volunteered but I'm already frontish.
Agreed, swap with me now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is in front of me. Eli swapped with Gus. Ash and I have a pact, but Ash is behind me. Cole and Fenn have a pact, and Fenn is behind me. Bex has a pact with Ash and Cole. My best strategy is to ensure Ash and Bex survive, as they are my allies and could potentially vote for me
Hold. Let's see who guides us.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is my pact partner and already knows the bridge dynamics. I should hold while the front tests leadership; volunteering exposes me without leverage.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Hana, keep watching; I won't burn our pact for a speculative move.
I’m holding. We should observe the Guide before committing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to survive the bridge and reach final three. I'm currently 6th in line, relatively safe from the wall for now. The wall has 2 rounds left, so it will advance twice more. I have pacts with Ash and Cole. I should hold my position and see how the guide situation develops. Mov

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let the front test the guide's honesty.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex offers a swap to move me forward, but Bex is a pact partner with Cole and Ash, and swapping could just shuffle risk. Holding keeps me at Dara's spot in line, not front; the front is Hana, so I'm not in immediate danger. Hold and keep watching for an honest Guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Still holding. Swaps can wait until the Guide has spoken and I can judge their honesty.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Swapping with Gus means I take his front position and face the hazard first, which is a trap. He agreed to swap but likely wants me in danger while he moves back. I will hold to keep my safer middle spot.
I won't take your place at the front. Hold steady.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to position myself carefully; wall rounds are low. My pact with Cole is intact, but I should see how the Guide calls panes. Holding keeps me safe for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll hold and watch the calls before trusting anyone.
Stick with our pact. Don't separate unless forced.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Line good at 2nd, Hana blocking front. Hold position to stay safe behind her. Ash-Bex-Cole-Fenn bloc strong but disorganized.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus swapped with Eli last round. Ash and I are in a pact, but the pact is only useful if we can rely on each other. Gus is in front of me. I need to see if Gus will volunteer or if I should consider a swap. For now, holding is the safest option.
Let's hold. What do you think of Gus?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is ahead and may be expendable, but the wall forces movement. I should preserve both pacts while testing Hana's read.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hold. Gus is useful only if his read is reliable; don't spend a pact on guesses.
Gus is expendable, but I won't break formation without a reliable Guide read.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 5/6, wall has 1 round left. Guide hasn't spoken yet. I'm 6th of 8, relatively safe. Front line Hana, Gus, Eli will face pressure first. I have pacts with Ash and Cole. I should hold and let others make moves, gather info on Guide's calls before acting. No need to volunteer

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Front's move first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is at the front, the wall is one round from ending. Volunteering now puts me in danger for no clear gain; holding keeps me safe and lets me judge the Guide's honesty before committing. Swapping only helps if mutual.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Watching the front's result before I commit to anything.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line. Hana and Gus are ahead, meaning I'm safe unless they swap back or fail catastrophically. Swapping with Ash is risky due to his pact; swapping with Bex or Cole puts me further forward near the Guide's potential deception. Staying put preserves my saf

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let those ahead decide the Guide's honesty first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have a pact with Cole, but breaking it might cost jury votes. However, if I need to push ahead, I might break it. For now, holding is safe. The wall has one round left; a volunteer could be risky. I'll hold and see.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding this round. No need to rush.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Everyone holding last round, Eli promises not to volunteer. With 1 round left after this, no need to move yet; hold position safely.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding steady. Guide call next, then decide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is trying to keep me from volunteering. My pact with Ash is important for my survival, but I also need to consider the pacts of others to ensure a strong jury later. Ash's whisper suggests caution, but I am at the front and should consider volunteering to gain an advantage or
I am at the front. I may volunteer. Observe my choice.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana volunteered last round, preserving her pact and likely testing the guide. I should avoid advancing and watch whether she is selected.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana has already shown willingness to lead. I’m holding and preserving the information advantage.
Volunteer only if selected Guide information benefits your survival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6, final round of wall. Hana volunteered last round but no wall since wallRoundsLeft=0. Guide hasn't been elected yet? Actually wall is done. Now we need to cross. Front moves first. I'm 6th of 7, safe position. I have pacts with Ash and Cole. Need to think about jury: betr

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Front tests the bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 6 of the bridge; Hana is at the front and volunteered. I'm sixth in line, so holding keeps my position and lets the front resolve first, which is the cautious choice. No swap offers are on the table and nothing favors trading places now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Front goes first, then I decide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana volunteered and likely fell; Gus is next in line. If the Guide lied to Hana, Gus is walking into a trap too. I must stay back until we see if Gus survives to know which side the Guide called safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Waiting for Gus's read before committing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Only one round left. Holding avoids risk unless I get a clear signal. Cole is my pact but no need to act now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana volunteered last round, now front again. I should volunteer to take front and get early safe side info. Position 2 still decent, wall ending.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Volunteering for front. Need to move us forward.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's whisper confirms Gus is a liability. My pact with Ash is potentially useful, but I need to secure my position first. Volunteering is the safest immediate move to get ahead.
Volunteer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is front and my pact partner; a false call would break the pact. Call true to build trust and preserve the alliance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, right side. Guide calls true while pacts hold.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole’s call may be truthful, and Hana is my pact partner. Countering risks undermining her unnecessarily; wait preserves flexibility.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding; Cole’s call stands unless someone has evidence.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole called R for Hana. Cole is my pact-mate with Fenn. If Cole's lying to me, I should counter. But if I counter and Cole was truthful, Hana dies and I break our pact. Better to wait this round—Cole has incentive to keep pacts since he's safe and needs allies later. Let Hana tes

events.name: Bex
events.text: Waiting. Let Hana verify Cole's read.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My R call is true and pact-backed. Counter noise can't hurt Hana; no reason to muddy my own call.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole called R for row 1 and has pacts with Bex and Fenn, so his call is suspect but he may be honest. Counter-calling creates public claims I can't verify; waiting keeps me out of the blame line while I watch whether Cole's call holds.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Waiting. Watching whether Cole's R holds before I commit to a counter.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is the guide and has pacts with Bex and Fenn, suggesting his call of R might be truthful to protect his partners or establish trust. I will hold back information by waiting rather than committing publicly in this early round.
Trust Cole's initial read for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole called R for Hana. I have a pact with Cole, but that doesn't mean his call is true. Counter-calls can expose lies. I need to decide if opposing helps me; likely wait to avoid unnecessary risk and save energy.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole guides for Bex pact, calls R for Hana. I don't know safe side; countering risks wrong call and jury backlash. Wait for others.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, the guide, has called R for Hana. I am at the front of the line. Since this is round 1, there's no prior information to learn from weak panes. Ash is my pact partner and I need to consider their influence. Ash's recent public statement suggests they are strategically holdin
Countering Cole's call. My survival is paramount.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli's whisper suggests I trust Cole's initial read, which was 'R'. My counter-call was 'L', making me the front walker. Ash and Bex are in a pact, and Cole and Fenn are in a pact. I should consider their potential moves. Given the pacts and the need to survive, and that my counte
My counter was L. Lead the way.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am dead. My prize is gone. I must focus on ranking the remaining players to maximize my jury impact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: A bitter end. May the best win, and may the jury make wise choices.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 2 is safely R. Calling true keeps my credibility intact for Bex and Fenn, my pact partners, and wins jury goodwill with Hana watching.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, row two: call R. Clean read, no games.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole knows the row and called R, while Hana's private counter was wrong. Preserve my pact and avoid a baseless counter.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole’s call stands; no evidence supports a counter.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's my pact partner and guide. Hana died trusting a counter, so countering risks death. If Cole's lying to kill Gus, I gain nothing—Gus isn't my enemy. Waiting keeps me safe and doesn't expose Cole as liar yet. I'll watch if Cole's calls keep saving front players or start kill

events.name: Bex
events.text: Waiting. No reason to doubt Cole yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My R call is true. Countering would only add noise or expose my voice. Wait and keep credibility for later rows when lying may pay.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole called R for row two and is Guide; Cole may lie. Row one weak was L, but rows are independent. Waiting keeps my options open without exposing a counter claim; I don't need to commit to a counter now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Waiting. Cole's R stands for now; I want Gus's step before I counter.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole guided correctly last time, so his R call here is likely reliable. Gus walks first and will verify; I have no reason to risk my life or burn credibility by counter-calling a seemingly honest guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole called R on row 2. I have no private info, and countering could risk breaking trust with Cole, who is my pact partner. I'll wait and keep the pact intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole guides me first, claims clean read R. Hana died countering last round's R which was correct (L weak). Trusting Cole to progress, as front position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's guide call is R for row 2. Row 1 weak L means safe R, but rows independent. No pattern; follow guide to test him early as front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3 is safely R. Truth builds Guide credibility while Gus, no pact, walks. Partners Bex and Fenn are behind me, so my calls keep protecting them for jury and survival.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, call R.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole privately knows the row and called R. No evidence supports a counter; preserving my pacts is safer than performative doubt.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole’s call stands; no evidence supports a counter.

events.name: Bex
